llm_input: Explain why the sky appears blue during the day.
llm_output: The sky appears blue during the day because of a phenomenon called Rayleigh scattering.Sunlight looks white, but it actually contains all the colors of the visible spectrum, from red to violet.When sunlight enters Earth's atmosphere:1. Sunlight interacts with air molecules, primarily nitrogen and oxygen.2. Shorter wavelengths scatter more strongly than longer wavelengths. Blue and violet light scatter much more than red and orange light.3. Blue light spreads across the sky, reaching our eyes from many different directions.Why isn't the sky violet?Violet light has an even shorter wavelength than blue, so it scatters more strongly. However, our eyes are less sensitive to violet light, and sunlight contains less violet than blue light.As a result, we perceive the sky as blue.Why are sunsets red and orange?During sunset, sunlight travels through a longer stretch of the atmosphere. Much of the shorter-wavelength blue light gets scattered away from the direct path, leaving more red and orange light to reach our eyes.In short: The sky is blue because Earth's atmosphere scatters shorter wavelengths of sunlight more strongly, causing blue light to reach our eyes from all directions.
